title: Audi India to raise prices by up to 2% from January 2027
body: Audi India will raise ex-showroom prices by up to 2% across its range from January 1, 2027, citing higher input costs. Brand Director Balbir Singh Dhillon said: "In response to rising input costs, we will be implementing a price revision of up to 2 per cent." It is Audi's second hike of 2026, after up to 2% on April 1. The page says Maruti Suzuki raised select models by an estimated weighted average of 0.31% from November 22, and Hyundai announced increases of up to ₹8,000 from December 1. Mercedes-Benz India plans a January 2027 hike too. The page carries no buyer reactions. The pattern of repeated small hikes across carmakers is what buyers are likely to notice.

title: Influencer fees aren't falling, but brands are demanding more for their money
body: Storyboard18 reports that India's influencer market is going through 'pricing rationalisation'. More creators means more competition, but that is not necessarily pushing fees down. Brands are judging creators on engagement quality, audience relevance and campaign performance rather than follower counts. In crowded categories like beauty and lifestyle, creators are adding extra posts or longer campaigns when a collaboration underperforms. Creators with established niches keep their pricing power. The page gives no fee figures and says Amazon-linked affiliate tools are unlikely to replace fixed fees soon. It expects a hybrid of guaranteed pay plus performance incentives.

title: Ranveer Singh and Aman Gupta launch men's grooming brand H.I.M
body: Launched on November 17, H.I.M debuted with eight products priced from ₹299 to ₹899: face wash, face cream, sunscreen, body wash, body lotion, shampoo, hair serum and an exfoliating soap bar. It sells on its own website, Amazon and Blinkit. Ranveer Singh said many grooming products he had used were not made for "Indian skin, weather and water conditions". Aman Gupta cited an 850% rise in searches for men's skincare routines over five years. A brand film features both co-founders. The page does not report any public pushback, and the celebrity-led launch lands in a crowded men's grooming market.

title: Shrinkflation: smaller packs, higher prices on everyday FMCG goods
body: Citing a Mint report, the article says companies have cut the weight of smaller packs of biscuits, chips, noodles, soaps and detergents by about 2% to 7%. A ₹10 noodle pack fell from 52 g to 48 g, and a ₹60 pack from 300 g to 280 g. Rs 5 chips and namkeen packs from two major brands fell from 25-30 g to 11-14 g over three years. Detergent prices rose by up to 11%, for example a 1 kg Quick Wash pack from Rs 235 to Rs 245. Companies say input costs rose about 8% to 9%. Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart favour larger packs because small ₹5 and ₹10 packs are uneconomical to deliver. The page frames this as a trust issue for shoppers who feel they are quietly getting less.

title: Myntra and Flipkart lose festive fashion share as rivals gain ground
body: Fynd's Festive Season Report 2026 says Myntra and Flipkart's combined share of festive fashion orders fell from 89% in 2025 to 76.8% in 2026. Myntra held 40.4% and Flipkart 36.4%, while AJIO had 7.3%, Amazon 5.5%, JioMart 3.8%, Nykaa 2.9% and Tata CLiQ 2.3%. Average festive discounts rose from 34% to 46%. Tier II cities made up about 35% of orders, up from 19% last year. The report covered over 65 brands across eight marketplaces in September and October. Shoppers outside the big metros and deeper discounts are driving the shift.

title: Madras High Court bars Blinkit from using CSK superfan's likeness in ad
body: The Madras High Court restrained Blinkit, The Times of India and unknown defendants from using the persona of Chennai Super Kings fan Saravanan Hari without his written permission. He sought ₹1.01 crore in damages over a Blinkit ad showing a cartoon of a yellow-painted fan. Bar & Bench tags the case under personality rights. Other reports say Blinkit argued the characters were fictional, and that the ad ran in the Chennai edition of the Sunday Times of India. The next hearing is on December 14, per Inc42's coverage of the case. The case has people asking whether ordinary fans have rights over how brands use their image.

title: Urban Company opens ₹2,500 Cr QIP, earmarks ₹600 Cr for 10-minute InstaHelp
body: Urban Company opened a ₹2,500 Cr QIP and plans ₹600 Cr over three years for InstaHelp, its 10-minute household services arm. InstaHelp's adjusted EBITDA loss was ₹305.96 Cr in H1 FY27, already above its ₹234.76 Cr loss for all of FY26. Average order value fell to ₹123 from ₹165 on lower introductory prices and competition. Rival Snabbit reported an FY26 net loss of ₹167.8 Cr on operating revenue of ₹12.2 Cr. Urban Company shares closed 5.80% lower at ₹161.65 on the BSE. The quick-service home help fight is drawing heavy spending.

title: D2C jewellery brand GIVA raises ₹975 Cr led by Multiples PE
body: Bengaluru-based GIVA raised ₹975 Cr (about $103 Mn) led by Multiples Alternate Asset Management, with Epiq Capital and Edelweiss Discovery Fund also taking part. FY26 revenue was ₹865 Cr, up from ₹505 Cr in FY25. It has about 425 stores and plans 160 more in FY27, focused on Tier II and III cities. Offline is about 45% of revenue, with a target of 75-80% in three years. Silver is about 60% of revenue. The CEO says it expects PAT-level profitability in FY28. A D2C brand moving into physical stores is the story people are noting.

title: Razorpay gets SEBI nod for IPO at about $5 Bn valuation
body: Razorpay has received SEBI approval for its IPO, targeting a raise of INR 5,500-6,500 crore at an expected valuation of USD 5 billion. That is below the USD 7.5 billion from 2021. It confidentially filed its DRHP in June 2026, and final IPO papers are expected before March 2027. Founders Harshil Mathur and Shashank Kumar started the company in 2014. It reversed flip to India and paid around USD 150 million in taxes on the move. The valuation reset against its 2021 peak is what market watchers are discussing.

title: Rediff files updated papers for ₹600 Cr fresh-issue IPO
body: Rediff.com India, a subsidiary of AvenuesAI, filed an updated DRHP dated November 13, 2026 for an IPO of up to INR 600 crore, all fresh equity. Proceeds include about INR 224.8 crore for Rediff One, Rediff Pay and Rediff TV, and INR 183.34 crore for marketing and branding. FY26 revenue was about INR 133.5 crore with operating profit of INR 65.24 crore. Borrowings rose to INR 399.26 crore as of June 30, 2026, from INR 7.74 crore in FY25, after a INR 400 crore acquisition. A once-famous email portal returning as an IPO candidate is the nostalgia hook. No IPO date or price band has been announced.

title: JioStar starts fresh layoffs, at least 150 roles
body: JioStar is starting a second round of job cuts affecting at least 150 roles in marketing, production, studios and operations, and sources say the final number could be higher. The earlier round cut over 1,000 roles after the Viacom18–Star India merger. Inc42's other report says affected staff get at least six months' salary and a pro-rata bonus. The page says Q2 FY27 EBITDA fell 11% year-on-year and margins shrank by 600 bps even as revenue and viewership rose. Heavy spending on content, sports rights and international expansion is weighing on finances. Media workers are noting that layoffs continue despite growth in subscribers.

title: India startup funding week Nov 2-7: 22 deals, $290M, EloElo raises $80M Series C
body: Indian startups raised $290.55 million across 22 deals in the week of November 2 to 7, plus 3 acquisitions. EloElo Group raised an $80 million Series C co-led by Hornbill Capital and NBCUniversal. Braid raised a $38 million Series A led by Octopus Ventures, and Clinics On Cloud $12.75 million. PowerUp Money raised a $10 million Series B. The funding is concentrated in a few large cheques. Social and consumer apps are still attracting money.

title: Dreamteam raises $53M; Blinkit court case; roundup of Nov 17 funding news
body: Dreamteam, an AI-first CRM company founded in 2025 by former Freshworks leaders, raised $53 million from Together Fund, Accel and Premji Invest. The roundup also covers Urban Company's QIP floor price of INR 161.03 per share with a discount of up to 5%. It notes the Madras High Court order against Blinkit and a separate ₹1.1 crore damages claim. Fresh AI-focused funding keeps arriving even as consumer-facing startups face scrutiny.

title: India's Diwali shopping spend set to fall 6 pc as inflation squeezes household budgets
body: The LocalCircles Mood of the Consumer survey projects urban festive spending at about ₹1.97 lakh crore in 2026, down 6% from ₹2.10 lakh crore last year. It drew more than 67,000 responses from 307 districts. 57% planned discretionary purchases and 31% planned to avoid them. Among planned buys, apparel, footwear and accessories led at 72%, and mobile phones and electronics were at 22%. 83% of households planning purchases expect to use savings for at least part of the spend. Retail inflation was 5.54% in September and food inflation was 7.74%. The article quotes no individuals. Its reading is that households have not stopped spending but are more deliberate, and that savings rather than stronger income are funding the spend.

title: Non-metro India drives 60% of new online shoppers amid shifting festive retail trends: KPMG
body: KPMG's 'India's Festive Retail Pulse 2026' says 60% of new online shoppers come from tier-II and tier-III markets. 57% of consumers plan discretionary festive purchases, and 86% use social platforms for shopping inspiration. Apparel, footwear and accessories remain the top festive category, while travel and experiences take a growing share of spending. The report describes buyers as cautious, focused on quality, value, convenience and experience. It says festive and wedding seasons are getting longer, so the opportunity is 'no longer defined by a single spending peak.' The Tribune notes this is a syndicated ANI feed that it does not verify.

title: The 10-minute delivery promise is losing its charm. Here's what Diwali shoppers actually want
body: A LocalCircles study of festive quick-commerce users found that 71% put best price or overall value first and 65% put product quality first. Only 22% named fast delivery. Six in 10 users say fees often make the final bill higher than expected. 69% typically spend ₹200–₹999 per order and 16% spend ₹1,000 or more. For last-minute festive shopping, Amazon Now was preferred by 22%, Blinkit by 19%, Zepto by 14% and BigBasket by 12%. Blinkit scored 5/5 for speed but 2.5 for value and transparency of charges. The article's theme is that shoppers now ask what they get for their money, not just how fast it arrives.

title: Gold Sales Reach ₹60,000 Crore On Dhanteras 2026, Buyers Shift To Lightweight Jewellery And Smaller Coins
body: Dhanteras gold sales are estimated at about ₹60,000 crore, up 15-20% year-on-year, though the quantity sold is expected to be broadly unchanged. Delhi 24-carat gold was ₹1.46 lakh per 10 grams on 6 November, against a January peak of ₹1.83 lakh and ₹1.32 lakh last Dhanteras. Silver sales are estimated up 30% in value and 10% in volume. Buyers moved to lightweight pendants, bangles and chains and to 1-5 gram coins, and 18-carat jewellery was about half of sales at one jeweller. Old-gold exchanges helped fund purchases. Digital gold drew younger buyers, with purchases starting from ₹10 on one platform. The page carries no buyer quotes.

title: No longer just a Delhi problem: As Delhi-NCR air turns toxic, air purifier sales double across India
body: Amazon India said air-purifier sales doubled in the last week. Croma's volumes more than doubled in 2026, and Xiaomi India's sales grew nearly fourfold year on year. Delhi-NCR accounted for nearly 80 per cent of volumes until 2025, but Mumbai also sees higher demand when air quality is poor. Industry estimates value the market at ₹320 crore in FY25, projected to reach ₹1,000 crore by FY30. Amazon says shoppers now compare models by room size, filter type and live AQI sensors. Versuni India's Pooja Baid says buyers are purchasing earlier, a shift from panic-driven to proactive adoption, even though 2026 has had fewer severe pollution days than last year.

title: Auto industry posts record October sales as passenger vehicles cross 5-lakh mark; 2-wheelers grow 16%
body: SIAM data show October passenger vehicle sales at 5,19,060 units, up 12.4%, the first time they crossed 5 lakh in an October. Two-wheelers reached 25,77,810 units, up 16.1%. Scooters grew 31.6% to 10,96,756 while motorcycles grew 6.6% to 14,23,118. From April to October, passenger vehicles are up 25.5% at 30,82,634 units. SIAM Director General Rajesh Menon called it healthy demand and credited improved credit availability and replacement demand in rural and urban markets. These are wholesale dispatch figures, not retail sales. The article gives no buyer reactions.

title: IndiGo cuts 300,000 seats in November despite festive travel season
body: OAG data show IndiGo at 12.8 million seats in November, down from 13.1 million in October. Total domestic and international capacity is down 2.5% against November 2025, and domestic is down 3.3%. Air India has 3.3 million seats, down 12.8%. SpiceJet is down 28.8%, while Akasa Air is up 31.9%. Delhi seats fell 3% to 2.9 million. Airlines blame high jet fuel prices and geopolitical uncertainty, which they say have pushed up fares. The article contains no passenger comments. IndiGo CEO Willie Walsh says the third-quarter outlook stays positive on forward bookings.

title: India's Big Fat Wedding Season To Unlock ₹7.5 Lakh Crore, 52 Lakh Marriages Set To Spark Spending Frenzy
body: CAIT projects 52 lakh weddings between November 21 and December 15, 2026, generating about ₹7.5 lakh crore of business. That compares with an estimated ₹6.50 lakh crore in 2025 and ₹3.75 lakh crore in 2022. Retail goods account for about ₹4 lakh crore and services for ₹3.45 lakh crore. Jewellery is put at ₹1.2 lakh crore, apparel at ₹90,000 crore, catering at ₹75,000 crore and venues at ₹60,000 crore. Delhi-NCR alone expects about 5 lakh weddings worth ₹2.5 lakh crore. CAIT's Praveen Khandelwal calls weddings a 'major economic engine' and expects about 1.25 crore temporary and part-time jobs. These are trade-body projections, not audited totals.

title: Govt notifies new set of rules governing India's civil aviation sector, replacing colonial-era Aircraft Rules, 1937
body: The Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam, 2026 replaces the Aircraft Rules, 1937 and takes effect on 1 January next year. Scheduled airlines must set fares based on factors such as operating costs and submit tariff details to the DGCA. Airlines must also publish fares on their websites and digital platforms, which the article describes as more transparent pricing. The Centre can issue written directions in an 'extraordinary situation' in the public interest. The article gives no fare caps, refund amounts or compensation figures. It carries no public reaction, but it lands in a month when fares and capacity cuts were a talking point.

title: Big PF relief: EPFO cuts minimum balance to 10%
body: The EPFO board's 240th meeting, chaired by Mansukh Mandaviya, cut the minimum balance that must stay in EPF accounts from 25% to 10%. The waiting period for final PF withdrawal after job loss falls from 12 months to two months. About 6.32 lakh members aged above 55 with accumulations above Rs 5 lakh are expected to benefit first. EPFO also reported automatic claim processing at 71% (up from 39%) and a claim rejection rate of 7.82% (down from 23%). Average settlement time is 2.57 days, down from 11.15 days. The article carries no member reactions and describes the Labour Ministry statement without quoting it.

title: NPCI Standardisation of UPI Dispute Management Rules in URCS
body: NPCI circular OC No. 240/2026–27, issued on November 4, 2026, changes how UPI disputes are handled. The revised rules take effect in URCS on November 25, 2026. 'Wrong Credit Chargeback' is renamed 'Wrong Payment – Reversal Request', and new reason codes cover excess charges, duplicate transactions, returned goods and defective or undelivered goods or services. Evidence such as payment receipts, purchase invoices and FIR/NCRP copies may be needed depending on the category. Banks must update their systems. This is a regulatory summary with no user reactions.

title: 50% work from home in Delhi-NCR till 20 November: Who's covered and who isn't
body: A CAQM order dated 30 October lets government and private offices in Delhi, Gurugram, Faridabad, Sonipat, Ghaziabad and Noida keep no more than 50% of staff in the office from 5 to 20 November. Delhi's October average AQI was 166, the lowest October figure in eight years, but it hit 377 by 4 November. Industrial units and essential services are exempt, and dust-generating construction is restricted. The reports do not say how the 50% is chosen, what the penalties are, or whether the order will be extended. The article advises employees to check their employer's circular and ask HR if unsure. It carries no employee quotes.

title: New financial rules from November 2026: toll pass, pension and bank charges update
body: From November 1, residents within 20 km of a toll plaza can get a discounted annual pass if their private vehicle has a valid FASTag. It costs 1,500 rupees outside municipal limits and 3,000 rupees within city limits, and works for only one plaza. Pensioners must submit their life certificate by November 30 or risk suspension of payments. IndusInd Bank now charges 25 rupees for a failed ATM or POS transaction due to insufficient balance, and 50 rupees for a returned cheque. All three were previously free. The page carries no user reactions, and its PNB cash-withdrawal wording is garbled.

title: Financial Rules Changing From November 2026: From ITR Deadlines And Pensions To GST, Know 5 Key Changes
body: From November 1, PNB credit cards charge no late fee on dues up to Rs 500, and late fees are capped at Rs 1,200 for dues above Rs 50,000. Utility payments above Rs 50,000 in a billing cycle attract a 1% fee, capped at Rs 2,000 per transaction. Cash withdrawals cost 2.5% or Rs 400 at PNB ATMs, and 2.5% or Rs 500 elsewhere. The ITR deadline for audited taxpayers moved from October 31 to November 21, and oil companies review LPG cylinder rates on November 1. The piece is an explainer and quotes no cardholders.

title: US assures India of lower tariffs than rivals as trade deal talks drag on
body: Citing a Bloomberg report, Business Today says the US has assured India of lower tariffs than its trading peers under the proposed bilateral deal. The first phase will cover goods only, with services left for later rounds. Talks have run for nearly two years, and a framework agreed in February 2026 is still not formalised because of several US trade investigations. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal called the terms a 'very good deal' and said an announcement could come 'quite soon'. India says it will not compromise on dairy market access or allow genetically modified products, which matters to farmers and food prices.

title: Trump weighs fresh tariff hikes on India over industrial subsidies
body: The Free Press Journal reports that Trump is weighing new tariff hikes on India after US probes into industrial subsidies. The USTR launched probes into 16 economies in March, and six (China, the EU, India, Japan, South Korea and Mexico) were named as possible new targets by the coming summer. The USTR already imposed an additional 10% duty on Indian imports in July under the same provision. The first tranche of the India-US deal is targeted for completion by the end of the current financial year. The page says the move may affect the ongoing deal talks, which exporters in textiles, gems and similar sectors are watching closely.

title: Petrol and diesel prices hold steady across metros
body: Petrol and diesel prices were unchanged in major cities on 25 November 2026. Petrol is ₹102.12 a litre in Delhi, ₹111.21 in Mumbai, ₹113.51 in Kolkata, ₹107.76 in Chennai, ₹111.68 in Bengaluru and ₹116.15 in Hyderabad. Diesel is ₹95.20 in Delhi, ₹97.83 in Mumbai, ₹99.82 in Kolkata, ₹99.55 in Chennai, ₹99.56 in Bengaluru and ₹104.23 in Hyderabad. The page says the oil companies revise prices daily at about 6 am, driven by crude prices, the rupee-dollar rate, freight and taxes. For commuters, delivery riders and transporters, steady rates mean no new hit to the monthly budget.

title: Gold prices slide, festive buying turns to lighter jewellery and old-gold exchanges
body: The World Gold Council says gold fell 6.3% in October to US$3,913/oz, then slipped a further 1% to US$3,870/oz by 12 November. Retailer estimates put festive value demand up 15-25% year on year, with volumes roughly flat to slightly higher. Average festive prices were about 17% higher year on year. Buyers were more numerous but bought lighter pieces, and old-gold exchanges made up roughly 40-60% of sales at many retailers. Bar and coin buying was healthy, mostly in 0.5g-5g sizes, which suggests families are stretching budgets for weddings.

title: Global tech layoffs hit 1.35 lakh in 10 months; Microsoft offers voluntary retirement to Indian staff
body: Layoffs.fyi data to 29 October shows 1,35,446 tech employees laid off across 334 companies this year, against 1,22,606 across 278 last year. About 93,217 of the cuts were attributed to AI. Amazon cut 16,000 jobs, Oracle 21,000, Dell 11,000 and Meta 10,400. Microsoft's voluntary retirement offer covers India: staff get one month's basic salary per year of service, with an opt-in deadline of 1 December. The article says Indian IT headcount has declined over successive quarters and entry-level hiring is being cut, so many freshers are anxious.

title: US H-1B extension rule would hit Indians hardest, USCIS data shows
body: A proposed US rule would end automatic deference to earlier approvals when H-1B petitions are extended. Indian-born workers received 79% of H-1B continuing-employment approvals in fiscal 2024, about 203,000 of 258,000. DHS estimates about 208,000 petitions a year would be affected. Petitions that got requests for evidence took 64 extra days to process on average, and DHS puts the added cost to petitioners at about $134,000 a year. The public comment period closed on 13 November, and Indian techies on H-1Bs are worried about the uncertainty.

title: GTA 6 launches and Shashi Tharoor tries it: 'not for me'
body: Rockstar's GTA 6 launched on 19 November, and the game became an online talking point in India. MP Shashi Tharoor tried it for the first time with a team member guiding him. He appeared entertained at first, but his interest faded, and he reposted the video on X with 'And I discovered GTA-6 is not for me!' His office's post called the first attempt 'decent (maybe)'. Online reactions were largely amused.

title: Did The Simpsons 'predict' a global blackout on 17 November?
body: A clip from the 2023 Simpsons episode 'It's A Blunderful Life' shows an older Lisa writing about a blackout in her diary, dated November 17. It resurfaced alongside a Microsoft outage and a scheduled US emergency alert test on the same date. One post tied it to the alert test, and commenters called it 'predictive programming'. Skeptics noted that Lisa's diary never mentions 2026, and X's AI assistant Grok called it a viral rumour mixing real events with fiction.

title: Schoolkids 'bunk' class for India vs New Zealand Test and hide from the camera
body: On day five of the first India-New Zealand Test in Wellington, schoolchildren in uniform appeared to have skipped class to watch the match. They were eating lunch at the stadium when they spotted the camera and covered their faces one by one. The article says entry to the final day was free. A clip posted by Sony LIV on Instagram went viral, and the children's reaction drew a lot of attention online.

title: Indian tourists in Norway spark debate on travel manners
body: Content creator Anirudh Kejriwal posted on X on 22 November about a Norway bus tour with a large group of Indian tourists. He said they sang Bollywood songs and played Antakshari at full volume, though about 70% of passengers were not Indian. He also described people skipping the queue, one tourist greeting the bus in Hindi, another bringing up Kashmir's crops during the guide's talk, and a loud family call. When he raised the singing, the reply was that the group should enjoy itself after travelling so far. The posts sparked a wider debate about balancing pride in one's culture with respect for shared spaces.

title: Japanese couple remarries in a Hindu wedding in Lucknow
body: Hiro Chihara and Shizu, a Japanese couple who divorced in 2022 and reunited in 2023, renewed their vows in a Hindu ceremony at Lucknow's Radha-Krishna Temple in Gomti Nagar on 23 November. They had come to the city for a friend's wedding two days earlier. They exchanged garlands, applied sindoor and took pheras, with Hiro in kurta-pyjama and Shizu in salwar-kurta. Their three children attended, and Indian friends had encouraged them to reconcile.

title: 'Chinese Spy Lookalike Contest' in New York goes viral over the Nvidia row
body: On 21 November, FactMachine and Prez held a costume contest at Washington Square Park in New York, with participants dressed as a Chinese spy. The event drew on the controversy around former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman. US intelligence officials reportedly believed she may have gathered information for Beijing, but her alleged spy role is not established, and China has rejected the allegations. The winner was due to get $50, about Rs 4,636. Reactions ranged from amusement to jokes that the participants might be real spies. The page timestamp is an update time.

title: Sikh man's self-funded 'onemillionfed' meals in Vancouver go viral
body: An Indian-origin Sikh man in Vancouver runs a self-funded food mission called 'onemillionfed', paying for every meal himself. He hides his face and doesn't share his name. In a viral Instagram video, a woman struggling with substance use tells him people should be less judgmental, and the exchange prompted discussion about stigma. The mission has also reached the langar kitchen at the Golden Temple in Amritsar, where he delivered supplies.

title: Foreign tourists on a restricted Taj Mahal watchtower: 13-second video circulates
body: On Wednesday 11 November, a foreign tourist couple reached Watchtower Number Four inside the Taj Mahal complex in Agra. The tower has an anti-drone surveillance system. A 13-second video of them on top circulated on social media, and the article calls it a 'major security lapse'. Suspicions point to a possible lapse in securing the entrance or negligence during a shift change, but the exact circumstances are not established. The ASI has sought a report.

title: India A lose to Pakistan A in Doha as on-field hostility and politics worry fans
body: India A met Pakistan A in the ACC Rising Stars Asia Cup 2026 in Doha. The match was tense, with verbal clashes and hostile send-offs, and India finished 48 runs short. The article says India-Pakistan matches at every level have been heavily politicised since the four-day conflict last May. Indian fan Mohammed Saeed Khan and Pakistani fan Abrar Hussain watched together. Hussain said 'Politics has poisoned cricket.' Khan thinks many players are 'forced into the act' by politicians and wants boards to discipline them. Doha resident Avinash Daniel said 'There are no different sides in the stands.'

title: Siraj dropped for first Test at Wellington, Shastri asks 'Where was MOHD SIRAJ?'
body: India left Mohammed Siraj out of the XI for the first Test at Wellington's Basin Reserve and played four pacers. Bumrah took 3 wickets, but New Zealand recovered from 70/5 to 243/5 at stumps. Henry Nicholls was 113 not out and Glenn Phillips 94 not out, in an unbroken 173-run stand. Ravi Shastri asked on X: 'Where was MOHD SIRAJ?' Batting coach Sitanshu Kotak said there was no fitness issue and that the XI was picked for the full five-day Test. Fans and former players have been arguing over the call.

title: IPL 2027: all 10 franchises finalise retentions before the December mini-auction
body: The 10 IPL franchises finalised their retained lists for IPL 2027. They retained 184 players, 55 of them overseas, and spent ₹1,002.05 crore. That leaves ₹297.95 crore in purses for the auction, with 66 squad slots open, 25 of them overseas. The article has no quotes. Its related headlines point to talk about Mohammed Shami possibly joining Rajasthan Royals and Rishabh Pant at Delhi Capitals.

title: Rohit and Kohli struggle in the New Zealand ODI series ahead of the 2027 World Cup
body: Khel Now says Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli struggled in the ODI series against New Zealand. Rohit made 30 runs in four innings, with two ducks. Kohli made 86 in four innings, including 74 off 51 balls in the first game and a duck at Mount Maunganui. India won the first two ODIs by DLS, the third was washed out, and Will Young's century plus Matt Henry's six wickets won the fourth for New Zealand. The piece says the numbers will raise concerns in the Indian camp before the 2027 World Cup. It has no fan quotes.

title: Gukesh holds Sindarov to a draw in Game 1 of the World Championship in Geneva
body: Game 1 of the 14-game FIDE World Championship match was played on 24 November in Geneva. It ended in a draw after 38 moves by threefold repetition, with the match score at 0.5–0.5 and 13 games to go. Gukesh, with Black, defended a Berlin endgame accurately against Sindarov. He had 6 minutes 32 seconds left on the clock against Sindarov's 15 minutes 51 seconds. The article calls his start solid and Sindarov's approach ambitious. Gukesh has White in Game 2. It has no direct quotes from either player.

title: India beat Pakistan 2-1 to win a third straight SAFF Championship
body: India came from behind to beat Pakistan 2-1 in the SAFF final in Dhaka. Pakistan led just before half-time. Junaid was sent off in the 59th minute, Bhat equalised soon after, and Mandi's 88th-minute header won it. It was India's 10th SAFF title, a record, and their third in a row. The AIFF posted 'Never count out the Blue Tigers.' Mandi said 'It's an amazing feeling!'

title: India lose 5-0 to New Zealand in football friendly in Auckland
body: India lost 5-0 to New Zealand at Go Media Stadium, their first-ever match in New Zealand. It was 3-0 at half-time. Bijoy Varghese's own goal opened the scoring, Jesse Randall scored twice and Chris Wood and Lachlan Bayliss added one each. Goalkeeper Vishal Kaith saved a 78th-minute penalty. Coach Khalid Jamil made five half-time changes. The match report has no fan comments.

title: India beat Japan 4-1 for a record sixth Asian Champions Trophy hockey title
body: In the final at Mohali, India were 1-0 down at half-time after Japan scored in the 3rd minute. They then scored four unanswered goals. Shilanand Lakra scored in the 42nd minute, Dilpreet Singh in the 48th, Jugraj Singh from a penalty corner and Vivek Sagar Prasad in the 54th. It was India's sixth title, a record, and completed a three-peat. The article has no fan reactions.

title: Ramayana Part 1 crosses ₹100 crore in two days, but Day 2 falls 25.9%
body: Per Sacnilk, Ramayana: Part 1 made ₹64.85 crore net in India on Day 1 and ₹48.05 crore on Day 2, a 25.9% drop. That is ₹112.90 crore net over two days and ₹221.05 crore worldwide gross. Early estimates had projected a near-₹100 crore opening. The reported budget is about ₹2,000 crore for Part 1. The article flags 'Mixed audience reactions' and suggests Dhanteras preparations may have kept some viewers out of theatres.

title: Ramayana jumps 91.5% on Day 5 despite mixed reviews
body: Ramayana: Part 1 made Rs 107.50 crore net in India on Day 5 (9 November), up 91.5% from Rs 56.15 crore on Day 4. Hindi accounted for Rs 87.25 crore of that. Sacnilk's worldwide total was Rs 663.90 crore. Reviews were mixed. Some viewers praised the concept and performances, including Yash as Ravana and Sai Pallavi as Sita. Others criticised the VFX.

title: Ramayana and Suriya's Scene make this the biggest Diwali week at the box office
body: Sacnilk estimates Ramayana and Suriya's Scene earned 1100+ crore worldwide in their first week. Ramayana made ₹930 Cr worldwide in 7 days and Scene ₹190 Cr in 6 days. Ramayana's Hindi business was supported by Kannada and Telugu dubs. Scene was strongest in Tamil Nadu and overseas, and drew interest in Kerala. The article has no audience quotes. It says the next test is whether people keep coming once regular working days replace the festive rush.

title: Suriya's Scene makes it three hits in 2026, with praise from Mahesh Babu and Atlee
body: Scene, released on 6 November, had a worldwide gross of Rs 1.75 billion as of 10 November, per Sacnilk. It is Suriya's third 2026 hit after Karuppu and Viswanath and Sons. Karuppu grossed nearly Rs 3 billion, and Kanguvaa was reportedly made on a budget of Rs 3-3.5 billion. Critics praised its offbeat humour. Mahesh Babu called it 'Cool, smart and so much fun' and Atlee praised its fresh narrative. The soundtrack's 'Aeroplane...' has more than 3 million Spotify streams.

title: Shah Rukh Khan's 'Tu Mil Jaaye' from King crosses 100 million plays
body: 'Tu Mil Jaaye' from King, released 2 November, passed 100 million combined views and plays on YouTube. It has been No. 1 on Ormax Heartbeats for two straight weeks and topped JioSaavn's charts. There are 283,000 reported Instagram Reels creations, and it was No. 6 on Apple Music Top 100 India on 19 November. The figures are promotional and not independently verified. DJs are adding it to party playlists, and fans are recreating the hookstep at celebrations. King itself releases on 24 December 2026.

title: OTT roundup: Dhindora Season 2 tops Netflix India, critics call it short of Season 1
body: Covering 16–22 November, Sacnilk says Dhindora Season 2 topped Netflix India's weekly shows chart. India Today gave it 3/5 and critics were divided on whether it keeps the first season's charm. Campus Diaries Season 2 and Teen Tigada got 3/5, and Manglik got 3.5/5 from Indulge Express. Among films, The Vvaan on Prime Video got between 0.5 and 2.5 out of 5. On Netflix India's movie chart, 418 was No. 3, Haiku was No. 4, Daayra was No. 1 and Ranabaali No. 2. Vishwanath & Sons has spent 10 weeks in the top 10.

title: Google denies mass India layoffs, says 30 Cloud roles cut
body: Posts on X claimed there were 'huge' layoffs at Google India, and other users shared unverified claims that staff were panicking or had received notices. Google Cloud India's official account called the rumours 'totally inaccurate'. It said about 30 roles were eliminated in a small organisational change made the previous week, as work was re-prioritised. The article notes that Microsoft separately offered voluntary exit packages to about 60,000 employees, including eligible teams in India. The episode shows how fast layoff rumours spread among Indian tech staff.

title: Salesforce layoffs 2026: India employees report cuts, some put on garden leave
body: Employees claiming to work at Salesforce India posted on Blind that they had lost their jobs. One said they were told in a meeting with their manager and the employee relations team, and was 'struggling to process the development'. Reported exit terms include garden leave until February 1, 2027 and some packages equal to about 21 weeks of pay. The article says these are unverified employee accounts, not confirmed company policy, and the total number affected has not been established. Business Insider reported up to 30 weeks of base pay for eligible US staff, which may not apply in India.

title: Qualcomm's layoff double blow: 1,000 Indian jobs at risk, extra pay to exit early
body: More than 1,000 Indian roles are reportedly at risk at Qualcomm. That is an unconfirmed estimate, and Moneycontrol said it could be 5% to 6% of an estimated 20,000-person India workforce. Cuts reportedly began in Bengaluru on November 9. Reported severance is three months' base salary plus pay tied to years of service, with one extra month for those who sign within three days. A CEO memo dated October 20, reviewed by Reuters, calls it a 'performance-focused reduction'. Qualcomm did not respond to queries, and the article quotes no affected staff.

title: Layoffs and favouritism? Qualcomm's job cuts trigger questions over fairness
body: An analysis of Blind posts found that 47.7% of Qualcomm-related layoff discussions mentioned politics or favouritism. The article says this is significantly higher than for Meta, Microsoft and Uber. Another 34.2% focused on cost management or performance factors, and 87% of the conversations concerned India. Employees raised concerns about managerial discretion and alleged preferential treatment based on regional ties, language background or networks. Others asked whether remote workers, people on medical leave or those returning from maternity leave were more vulnerable. The article stresses the data shows employee perceptions, not proof of bias.

title: InnoData lays off nearly 550 employees in India, job cuts reported in the Philippines
body: Nearly 550 employees in India were reportedly laid off on October 26, 2026. InnoData has not confirmed the figure. Staff lost access to laptops and accounts during the workday, and one Delhi-based employee said 'One by one, we started losing access to our official devices.' Affected workers formed a WhatsApp group that had almost 500 members by late evening, 'all clueless and in a state of panic'. Employees said they got no HR call and could not download payslips before losing payroll access.

title: Microsoft announces voluntary exit offer for employees in India, 3 other countries
body: Microsoft offered a voluntary exit to eligible employees at level 70 and below in participating teams in India, the US, the UK and Canada. About 60,000 employees are eligible globally. Microsoft has about 23,000 employees in India, but it is unclear how many are eligible. Indian staff have until December 1 to decide. Severance is roughly one month's base salary per completed year of service, plus health insurance and career transition help. Chief People Officer Amy Coleman called the offer 'new for us' and said it gives eligible staff 'a new choice to make that transition now with support'.

title: 'Freshers are not disappearing, their jobs are changing': Cognizant India chief on AI hiring
body: Cognizant India's Rajesh Varrier said the story is 'role transformation rather than the disappearance of entry-level opportunity'. A June 2026 Cognizant-Pearson study found AI already performs 37% of entry-level tasks at Indian organisations, against a 33% global average. Cognizant plans to hire 24,000-25,000 freshers in 2026, about 20% more than the roughly 20,000 hired in 2025. Nasscom president Rajesh Nambiar said 'From a fresher's point of view, it is a concern, (and) I will not sugarcoat it any differently.' Cognizant's headcount was 359,900 as of September 30, 2026.

title: TCS employee alleges denial of office entry over Ayyappa Deeksha attire
body: An employee at TCS's Adibatla office in Hyderabad alleged he was stopped at the entrance on November 19 for wearing traditional attire while observing Ayyappa Deeksha. He says he told management nearly two months earlier about his religious vow. HR reportedly asked him to change into trousers, citing how international clients might perceive the attire. Ayyappa devotees and Hindu organisations protested outside, and the protest ended peacefully. Police called it 'a misunderstanding', ruled out a communal angle and said it was resolved. TCS had issued no public statement.

title: SBI to hire AI specialists: Can public-sector pay win the AI talent war?
body: SBI is hiring a Chief AI Officer with maximum annual compensation of Rs 1.6 crore. It is also recruiting five more AI specialists on fixed-term contracts, including deputy general managers and AI architects. Technology professionals on social media said the pay may not be competitive for a role of this scale. Some noted that comparable packages are common in private tech for experienced engineers and senior specialists. The article says demand for AI expertise is rising faster than many pay structures reflect market realities.

title: Meta tweaks Instagram recommendations in India to reduce suggestive, violent content
body: Meta said it changed how Instagram recommends content in India, limiting sexually suggestive and violent material from accounts users don't follow. The change follows a technology ministry advisory issued on October 10. Meta says reports about recommended content fell by nearly 50 percent over the past year, but gave no supporting figures. It says this changes what is promoted, not what is allowed, and it did not explicitly link the change to the advisory. The article quotes no users or critics, though Outlook India's coverage raised censorship and transparency questions.

title: LJP (Ram Vilas) seeks Delhi CM's intervention for FIR against comedian over Chhath remarks
body: A clip of stand-up comedian Yash Maheshwari's set, uploaded to his YouTube channel on November 21, drew widespread criticism and demands for legal action. His remarks about the sindoor worn by married women during Chhath Puja were called 'obscene and derogatory'. He apologised on November 24, but the LJP (Ram Vilas) says an apology alone is not enough. It asked for an FIR and for the venue and organisers to be investigated. It also asked Delhi Police to preserve the videos and limit their spread. The article quotes no individual online posts.

title: 'Har Ghar Pattinson': Indians are sure James Bond is coming for their jobs & pani puri
body: After Robert Pattinson was announced as the new James Bond, Indian social media filled with AI memes joking that he is taking over jobs and cultural icons. One AI edit put him in the Prime Minister's look. One X user asked 'If not Modi then who?' and answered 'Likely Robert Pattinson'. Others joked about a 'Har Ghar Pattinson Scheme', and a pani puri vendor reel and a Rameshwaram Cafe 'dosa master' post drew food-job jokes. The author reads the trend as a lighthearted way to talk about unemployment. The page header shows November 25, but the article was published November 21.

title: 'Social media couples are fake': Mythpat faces backlash after GTA 6 livestream clip
body: Gaming creator Mithilesh Patankar (Mythpat) was criticised after a GTA 6 livestream clip showed him repeatedly calling his wife Urmila Lawekar 'gadhi' during a controller dispute. He then asked her to apologise to his viewers, and she refused. A viral tweet claimed he said it 10 times, which the article presents as a social media claim, not a verified fact. Users called him disrespectful and a 'manchild'. One wrote 'Please say sorry to my sister Urmila'. Several said the clip proves 'social media couples are fake'. The article reports no response from Mythpat.

title: FSSAI faces criticism over Bisleri bottles seen at food safety training after announcing prosecution against the brand
body: Photos from a one-day FSSAI food safety training in Ghaziabad, attended by about 1,155 officials, showed Bisleri water bottles on tables. This came days after FSSAI announced on November 22 that it had sanctioned prosecution of Bisleri over a failed water sample. Bisleri said the issue involved one batch from its Goa plant tested in September 2025, and that five of six samples passed. Users called it a contradiction, and one wrote that 1,155 food safety officials and Bisleri on the table 'says a lot'. Another said they trusted the brand more than the regulator. The page shows an 'Updated' stamp of November 25, 6:08 PM IST, and no separate print date.

title: Stuck between two worlds: Rs 1.27 crore-earning man's search for the perfect wife goes viral
body: Jasveer Singh, CEO of Gurugram-based KnotDating, shared a matrimonial requirement on X from an IIT graduate earning Rs 1.27 crore a year. The man wants a partner who grew up in a small town and built a career in a metro. He calls this preference the 'Two Nation Theory', and says he has lived in metros for over a decade. The article says the post 'sparked discussion online' but does not describe what commenters said. The page shows an 'Updated' stamp of November 24, 8:13 PM IST.
